Daniel —

Appreciate the clarity. Quick answers up front: our standard hosted uptime is 99.90% and for Dedicated (reserved pools) we target 99.95% monthly. For pilot-oriented commercial offers we can discuss a bespoke baseline.

How we calculate credits (proposal):
- Measured monthly across the tenant region.
- If monthly uptime >= baseline, no credit.
- If uptime < baseline, credit = (baseline - actual uptime) / baseline * monthly invoice amount.

Example: baseline 99.95% and actual 99.50% => delta 0.45% -> credit = 0.0045 * monthly invoice.

We typically set a cap at 50% of the monthly invoice for large accounts; for pilots we can consider a lower cap. We can also exclude scheduled maintenance windows that are communicated 72 hours in advance and individually shorter than 2 hours.

I'm attaching an initial redline of our SLA with two alternate credit caps (25% cap and 50% cap) for you to review. Also attached a short CSV showing sample calculations for a few outage scenarios.

Attachments: Helion_SLA_redline_v1.pdf (redline), downtime-calculation-sheet.csv (sample math)

Would you be open to a 30-minute call tomorrow to run through numbers and your procurement constraints?

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Daniel —

Thanks for the fast feedback and for surfacing procurement's constraints. After internal alignment we can offer the following pilot SLA terms:

1) Baseline uptime: Hosted pilot 99.97% (subject to a 3-month pilot commitment); Dedicated 99.95% as standard.
2) Credit calculation: percentage-of-invoice formula as outlined previously.
3) Payout mechanism: default invoice credit; cash payout is available only if the monthly credit exceeds 25% of the monthly invoice and customer provides payment routing details in the SOW.
4) Monthly cap: 25% of the monthly invoice for pilot months.
5) Scheduled maintenance carveouts: up to 2 windows/month, each <= 2 hours, if communicated at least 72 hours in advance. Any scheduled window beyond that counts toward downtime.
6) Additional mitigation: we will enable a canary fallback policy (technical control) during the pilot to reduce incident exposure; details to be included in the operations exhibit.
